How to use a quote instead of just reading it

Pick one line that names something you are carrying. Write it where you will see it tomorrow: a sticky note, a lock screen, the top of a journal page. Then ask one question of it: what would today look like if I believed this? A quote becomes useful when it changes one small decision.

Common questions

Who said these quotes?

Each quote names its author, from Stoic philosophers and poets to writers and therapists. If you think an attribution is wrong, email hello@theraglee.com and we will check it.

Can I share these quotes?

Yes. Share the page, pin it, or copy a line. Please keep the author’s name with it.

Why are the quotes sorted by theme?

Because the line you need on an anxious morning is not the one you need in grief. The themes match the topics in Theraglee’s free tools and articles.

Do I need an account?

No. The page is free to read. A free account adds one quote a day on your dashboard alongside an affirmation, a tip and a fact.

Educational only — not medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. Find a licensed therapist if you want support.
